================================================================================
  FCPP PROJECT GENERATION PROMPT — Copilot Agent Template
  Based on: https://github.com/HeT-FTI/fcpp (A Modern System-level C/CPP Build)
================================================================================

Use this prompt with GitHub Copilot agent (or any code-gen agent) to scaffold a
new Conan 2 C/C++ library project from the HeT-FTI/fcpp template. Fill in the
[FILL] placeholders, then feed the entire file to the agent.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 1 — PROJECT IDENTITY  (fill every [FILL] below)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Project name        : [FILL e.g. mylib]
Version             : [FILL e.g. 0.1.0]
Team / Organization : HeT-FTI                          ← FIXED, do not change
Author(s)           : [FILL e.g. Jane Doe <jane@example.com>]
License             : Apache-2.0                       ← FIXED, do not change
One-line description: [FILL e.g. A high-performance image codec library]
Repository URL      : [FILL e.g. https://github.com/HeT-FTI/mylib.git]
Homepage            : [FILL e.g. https://github.com/HeT-FTI]
C++ standard        : 17                               ← FIXED team standard
C standard          : 11                               ← FIXED team standard
Build type          : [FILL Debug | Release]
Library type        : [FILL static (is_shared=false) | shared (is_shared=true)
                            | header-only (is_header=true)]
Enable Python bindings (pybind11) : [FILL true | false]
Enable code coverage              : [FILL true | false]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 2 — LIBRARY DESIGN  (describe what your package does)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Purpose & scope:
[FILL — Describe in 3-10 sentences what this library is for. What problem does
it solve? What domain does it serve (math, networking, image processing, etc.)?
This description drives what headers, classes, and functions the agent creates.]

Public C headers (include/*.h) to generate:
[FILL — List every C header you need, with a brief note on what each exposes.
Example:
  - codec.h      → C-interface for encode/decode functions
  - config.h     → Build-time configuration constants
If your library is C++-only, write "None".]

Public C++ headers (include/*.hpp) to generate:
[FILL — List every C++ header you need.
Example:
  - encoder.hpp  → Encoder class with stream-based API
  - decoder.hpp  → Decoder class, supports async decoding
  - types.hpp    → Shared enum/struct definitions]

Source files (src/*.c and src/*.cpp) to generate:
[FILL — List implementation files that pair with headers above. The fcpp
convention is one source per header (pairwise assumption).
Example:
  - codec.c      → implements codec.h
  - encoder.cpp  → implements encoder.hpp
  - decoder.cpp  → implements decoder.hpp]

Key classes / functions / data structures:
[FILL — Describe the main API surface the agent should create. Include:
  - class names, key methods, constructor signatures
  - free functions with parameter/return sketches
  - important enums or structs
Example:
  class Encoder {
    Encoder(Format fmt, int quality);
    void feed(const uint8_t* data, size_t len);
    std::vector<uint8_t> finish();
  };
  enum class Format { PNG, JPEG, WEBP };
]

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 3 — DEPENDENCIES
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Conan requirements (conandata.yml):
[FILL — List each dependency in "pkg/version" format.
Example:
  - "gtest/1.16.0"        (always keep for testing infra)
  - "zlib/1.3.1"
  - "opencv/4.9.0"
If none beyond GTest, write "gtest/1.16.0" only.]

Dependency → target mapping (metadata.json > dependencies):
[FILL — For each dependency, state which sub-targets to link and whether it
belongs to "common", "c", "cpp", or "infra".
Example:
  common : { "ZLIB": ["ZLIB::ZLIB"] }
  c      : {}
  cpp    : { "OpenCV": ["opencv::opencv_core", "opencv::opencv_imgproc"] }
  infra  : { "GTest": ["gtest::gtest"] }
]

Quality-gate sync (IMPORTANT): the clang-tidy CI gate installs system header
deps by mapping conandata.yml requirements (see .github/workflows/
security-linters.yml: zlib→zlib1g-dev, pcre2→libpcre2-dev, eigen→libeigen3-dev;
header-only ETL is downloaded at the version declared in conandata.yml). When
adding a new C/C++ dependency whose headers appear in src/, extend that mapping
(or add an ETL-style source download). Missing mapping = clang-tidy include
errors in CI (fail-loud by design). See het-deps for full dependency governance.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 4 — EDITABLE FILES & AGENT INSTRUCTIONS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The following files in the fcpp template are user-editable. The agent MUST
generate/modify each one according to the project design above.

4.1  metadata.json  (project-level configuration hub)
     ─────────────
     • Set "name", "version", "description", "authors", "maintainers",
       "topics", "url", "homepage" from Section 1.
     • "team" is always "HeT-FTI".
     • "license" is always "Apache-2.0".
     • "build_cppstd" is always "17".  "build_cstd" is always "11".
       These are team standards and MUST NOT be changed.
     • "generate_modules_inplace" is always false.
       C++23 module generation is experimental and not applicable under C++17.
     • Set "is_shared", "is_header", "enable_python_bindings",
       "activate_code_coverage" from Section 1.
     • Populate "dependencies" → common/c/cpp/infra from Section 3.
     • Set "cmake_version" to "4.2.3" (or newer). 4.2 is the floor for MSVC:
       below it CMake cannot name the Visual Studio generator Conan derives.
     • Set "trigger_tests" to true, "saving_tests_log" to true.
     • Set "workflow_triggers" to the team default (all six true):
         {"build": true, "tests": true, "release": true,
          "docs": true, "security_scan": true, "cross_compile": true}
       A switch grants PERMISSION, the gitmoji states INTENT. Handing every
       permission out up front is what keeps one skill document literally true
       in every derived project. build/test/docs/security gates are on by
       default (PR shift-left); cross_compile is decoupled (only
       :hammer_and_wrench: starts it, and it never runs on a PR); release needs
       BOTH the switch and the release gitmoji in the pushed commits.
     • Leave "build_type" at the project default ("Debug"). It is a declared
       project state, NOT a gate: no pipeline reads it, so never flip it in
       order to release.
     • Configure "doc_languages", "doc_versions", "doc_doxygen_folders",
       "doc_doxygen_suffix" as appropriate. Keep .dox/.cxx as documentation-only
       suffixes: every .dox/.cxx file must live under docs/doxygen/dox/, never
       under include/ or src/ (the suffix list applies to all folders, so it
       does not enforce this by itself).

4.2  conandata.yml  (dependency specs)
     ─────────────
     • List every requirement from Section 3 under `requirements:`.

4.3  include/*.h and include/*.hpp  (public headers)
     ──────────────────────────────
     • Create all header files listed in Section 2.
     • Every header MUST use the fcpp import-guard convention:
         // Conan::ImportStart
         #pragma once
         #include <...>
         // Conan::ImportEnd
     • Add Doxygen docstrings to every public class, function, enum, struct.
       Use @brief, @param, @return, @tparam.
     • KEEP @exporter and @attacher annotations in docstrings.
       Rationale: although C++17 does not use C++23 module generation, these
       annotations are lightweight (no build impact under C++17) and preserve
       forward-compatibility. When the team migrates to C++23 in the future,
       the codebase will already be properly annotated for automatic module
       export — avoiding a costly retrofit across every source file.
       Convention:
         - @exporter on standalone declarations in headers (free functions,
           class declarations, template instantiations).
         - @attacher on member-function definitions in source files.
     • Support multi-language docstrings with [en]/[zh] tags if the user's
       doc_languages includes both. Otherwise English-only is fine.

4.4  src/*.c and src/*.cpp  (implementations)
     ─────────────────────
     • Create all source files listed in Section 2.
     • Every source file MUST use the fcpp import-guard convention:
         // Conan::ImportStart
         #include "myheader.hpp"
         #include <third_party.h>
         // Conan::ImportEnd
     • Add Doxygen @brief + @exporter / @attacher to every function definition.
       (Same forward-compatibility rationale as 4.3.)

4.5  test_package/main.cpp  (benchmark & validation program)
     ─────────────────────
     PURPOSE: This is a BENCHMARK program that validates the completeness of
     the built package. It acts like a generic benchmark: run every kernel API,
     measure wall-clock time cost, and print a summary table.

     AGENT INSTRUCTIONS:
     • #include all public headers from the library.
     • For every public function / class / key API:
       1. Call the API with representative inputs.
       2. Wrap the call with std::chrono::high_resolution_clock to measure
          elapsed time (microseconds or milliseconds).
       3. Print a one-line result: API name, status (PASS/FAIL), time cost.
     • At the end of main(), print a summary table like:

         ======================== Benchmark Summary ========================
         API                     Status    Time (ms)
         ─────────────────────── ──────── ──────────
         encode()                PASS      12.34
         decode()                PASS       8.91
         ...
         ====================================================================

     • Return 0 on all-pass, non-zero if any API fails.
     • If resource files are needed, read from "./resources/" (copied by the
       Conan test harness via RESOURCES_PATH).

4.6  test_package/test/unit/*.cpp  (GTest unit tests)
     ────────────────────────────
     PURPOSE: Fine-grained correctness tests. Each .cpp file maps to one or
     more logical test suites (TEST(Suite, Case) macros).
     AGENT INSTRUCTIONS:
     • Create one test file per public header/source pair. Name it after the
       header, e.g. test_encoder.cpp for encoder.hpp.
     • #include <gtest/gtest.h> and the header under test.
     • Cover: constructor behavior, normal input/output, edge cases, error
       handling, template instantiations.
     • DO NOT add a main() — the framework auto-generates it at build time.
     • If the function under test needs resource files, use the RESOURCES_PATH
       macro (provided via CMake compile definition) to locate them.

4.7  test_package/test/stress/*.cpp  (GTest stress / performance tests)
     ──────────────────────────────
     PURPOSE: Long-running or resource-intensive tests (large data, timing,
     concurrency).
     AGENT INSTRUCTIONS:
     • Create stress test files for performance-critical functions.
     • Use std::chrono for timing, std::thread for concurrency tests.
     • DO NOT add a main() — same auto-generation as unit tests.

4.8  test_package/resources/  (test resource files)
     ───────────────────────
     • Place any data files needed by test_package/main.cpp or test cases.
     • Example: sample input files, golden-output reference files, configs.
     • These are copied to the build folder at test time.

4.9  api/python_bindings.cpp  (pybind11 bindings — if enabled)
     ───────────────────────
     • If enable_python_bindings is true:
       - #include <pybind11/pybind11.h>, <pybind11/stl.h>, and project headers.
       - Bind every public class, function, enum using PYBIND11_MODULE.
       - For template functions/classes, bind each concrete instantiation.
       - Name the module "<project_name>_python".
     • If disabled, leave this file as a placeholder or remove it.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 5 — DOCUMENTATION SYSTEM
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

The fcpp template has a dual Doxygen + Sphinx documentation pipeline invoked
via `python ./docs/build.py`. The agent must generate:

5.1  Doxygen docstrings  (inline in headers + sources, see 4.3 / 4.4)
     ────────────────────
     Every public symbol must have a Doxygen comment block including:
       @brief   — one-line summary (with optional [en]/[zh] variants)
       @param   — for each parameter
       @tparam  — for each template parameter
       @return  — return value description
       @note, @warning, @see, @since, @version — as appropriate
       @exporter / @attacher — KEEP these annotations for forward-compatibility
         with future C++23 module migration (see Section 4.3 rationale)
       @ingroup — assign to a logical Doxygen group
     Use the doctest.hpp example in the template as the style reference.

5.2  docs/doxygen/dox/mainpage.dox  (Doxygen landing page)
     ─────────────────────────────
     • HARD REQUIREMENT: exactly one @mainpage must exist, or the docs cannot
       be built at all (docs/build.py fails the build otherwise).
     • Rewrite the mainpage to reflect the new project: name, purpose, quick
       usage snippet, feature list.
     • Support [en]/[zh] @section tags if multi-language.
     • @since tag should match the initial version.

5.3  docs/doxygen/dox/demos/*.dox + *.cxx  (Doxygen example pages)
     ────────────────────────────────────
     • HARD REQUIREMENT: demos/ must exist and hold at least one tutorial .dox
       with @example -- that tutorial plus the mainpage is what makes the doc
       set "complete".
     • SOFT: the example code. For each major feature create a .dox with the
       explanatory docstring and 0..N .cxx files it pulls in via @include.
       Several .cxx per .dox is normal; no 1:1 pairing is required.
     • Use @example, @code{.cpp} / @endcode, @ingroup as in the template.
     • IMPORTANT: .dox and .cxx are documentation-only. They live exclusively
       under docs/doxygen/dox/ and must never be created under include/ or
       src/, which carry .h/.c/.hpp/.cpp only. A .dox/.cxx in those trees is a
       layout violation (see docs/doxygen/dox/ for the canonical set).

5.4  Sphinx documentation  (index.rst as a mini journal paper)
     ─────────────────────

     DESIGN PHILOSOPHY:
     Think of index.rst as a SHORT JOURNAL PAPER for new users. It must be
     concise and clear — a reader should understand what this library does,
     why it matters, how to use it, and what results to expect, all within
     a single focused page. The structure is:

       1. BACKGROUND    — What problem does this library solve? Why does it
                          exist? (2-4 sentences)
       2. METHOD        — What approach / algorithm / technique is used?
                          Keep it brief — just enough for users to understand
                          the core idea. (a short paragraph or bullet list)
       3. QUICK START   — How to install and run a minimal working example.
                          (code block with conan create / #include / usage)
       4. RESULTS       — What does the user get? Show expected output,
                          screenshots, or performance numbers.
                          (figures, tables, or sample stdout)
       5. LICENSE        — One-line pointer to LICENSE file.

     CONSTRAINT: index.rst must stay SHORT. If any section (especially Method
     or Results) requires lengthy explanation, SPLIT it into a separate .rst
     and link via toctree. For example:
       - Method is complex → create method.rst, link from index.rst
       - Multiple subsystems → create one .rst per subsystem
     The goal: index.rst is always scannable in under 2 minutes of reading.

     ADAPTIVE LAYOUT based on library complexity:

     SIMPLE LIBRARY (few headers, single-purpose):
       • A single index.rst following the mini-paper structure is sufficient.
       • No additional .rst files needed.

     COMPLEX LIBRARY (many headers, distinct submodules / subsystems):
       • index.rst remains the concise mini-paper landing page.
       • Add additional .rst files as needed and link via toctree:
           - method.rst       → deep-dive into algorithms / theory
           - <module>.rst     → per-submodule documentation
           - cmake.rst        → CMake build options reference
           - conan.rst        → Conan recipe options reference
           - meta.rst         → metadata.json field reference
           - benchmark.rst    → detailed benchmark tables & analysis
       • Let the content decide the structure — don't create empty pages
         just for the sake of structure.

5.5  Sphinx internationalization  (CRITICAL — auto-translate .po files)
     ───────────────────────────
     The Sphinx system supports multi-language builds via sphinx-intl. If
     metadata.json "doc_languages" includes any language besides English
     (e.g. ["en", "zh"]), the agent MUST generate translation files.

     LANGUAGE TAG MAP (used by conf.py and docs/build.py):
       en → en
       zh → zh_CN
       jp → ja

     FOR EACH NON-ENGLISH LANGUAGE in doc_languages:
       1. Create locale directory structure:
            docs/sphinx/locales/<lang_tag>/LC_MESSAGES/
          Example for Chinese: docs/sphinx/locales/zh_CN/LC_MESSAGES/

       2. For EVERY .rst file in docs/sphinx/source/ (including those in
          subdirectories like components/), generate a corresponding .po file:
            docs/sphinx/locales/<lang_tag>/LC_MESSAGES/<rst_name>.po
          Example: index.rst → locales/zh_CN/LC_MESSAGES/index.po
                   method.rst → locales/zh_CN/LC_MESSAGES/method.po

       3. Each .po file MUST follow standard gettext format:
            # SOME DESCRIPTIVE TITLE.
            # Copyright (C) <year>, HeT-FTI
            # This file is distributed under the same license as the <name> package.
            #
            #, fuzzy
            msgid ""
            msgstr ""
            "Project-Id-Version: <project_name> <version>\n"
            "Report-Msgid-Bugs-To: \n"
            "POT-Creation-Date: <date>\n"
            "PO-Revision-Date: YEAR-MO-DA HO:MI+ZONE\n"
            "Last-Translator: FULL NAME <EMAIL@ADDRESS>\n"
            "Language: <lang_tag>\n"
            "Language-Team: <lang_tag> <LL@li.org>\n"
            "Plural-Forms: nplurals=1; plural=0;\n"
            "MIME-Version: 1.0\n"
            "Content-Type: text/plain; charset=utf-8\n"
            "Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit\n"
            "Generated-By: Babel 2.17.0\n"

       4. For each translatable text block in the .rst, add a msgid/msgstr pair.
          THE AGENT MUST FILL IN the msgstr with the ACTUAL TRANSLATION in the
          target language. Do NOT leave msgstr empty — that defeats the purpose.
          Example for zh_CN:
            msgid "Introduction"
            msgstr "简介"

            msgid "This library provides high-performance image codecs."
            msgstr "本库提供高性能图像编解码功能。"

       5. After creating the .po files, also generate the compiled .mo files.
          If the agent cannot generate binary .mo files, at minimum generate all
          .po files with translations filled in, and note that `msgfmt` must be
          run to compile them (or `python ./docs/build.py` will handle it).

     IMPORTANT: The docs/build.py automation calls sphinx-intl to generate
     locale scaffolding, but the TRANSLATIONS themselves must be human- or
     agent-written in the .po files. The agent must auto-fill msgstr fields.

5.6  docs/images/  (static images for documentation)
     ────────────
     Naming convention:
       IN_*.jpg/png  → Doxygen-only figures
       OUT_*.jpg/svg → Sphinx-only figures
       ALL_*.jpg/png → shared by both systems

     MANDATORY FILE:
       docs/images/ALL_title_card.png
       This image is REQUIRED. It serves as the project's cover card in the
       HeT-FTI/HeT-AI-Gallery aggregation portal
       (https://het-fti.github.io/HeT-AI-Gallery/).
       The Gallery's index.html searches for ALL_title_card.png (or .jpg etc.)
       in each project's Sphinx _images/ output to display as the card image.
       If this file is missing, the Gallery falls back to a generic placeholder.

       The agent should generate a placeholder ALL_title_card.png (or note that
       the user must provide one). Recommended dimensions: ~600x400px, showing
       the project name/logo and a brief visual hint of what the library does.

     • Also place: logo, demo screenshots, architecture diagrams as needed.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 6 — OTHER FILES FOR PROJECT COMPLETENESS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

6.1  README.md
     • Rewrite with: project name, badges (CI, license, C++ std, docs),
       overview, features, build requirements, crash course, project structure
       tree, license section. Follow the existing template's README style.

6.2  LICENSE and NOTICE
     • DO NOT MODIFY. These files are inherited from the HeT-FTI/fcpp template
       and are governed by the organization's legal terms.
     • LICENSE: Apache License 2.0 — must remain as-is.
     • NOTICE: Contains copyright and CC BY-NC 4.0 documentation license
       attribution for Shenzhen HeT Intelligent Control Co., Ltd. — must
       remain as-is.

6.3  .gitignore
     • Keep existing patterns. Add project-specific ignores if needed
       (e.g., model weights, large data files).

6.4  (retired)  the old `build` one-liner script
     • Deleted from the template: README section 3 inlines the same commands, so
       there is no longer a package-name or build-type literal to hand-edit.

6.5  Doxyfile
     • No manual edits needed — it uses %PLACEHOLDER% tokens filled by
       docs/build.py at build time. Only touch if adding custom Doxygen config.

6.6  conanfile.py / CMakeLists.txt / test_package/conanfile.py /
     test_package/CMakeLists.txt
     • These are FRAMEWORK FILES — do NOT modify them unless you have a
       structural reason (e.g., adding a new build target type). The template's
       automation reads metadata.json and conandata.yml to drive everything.

6.7  .github/misc/.releaserc.json  (semantic-release config)
     • NO manual edits needed: the repository URL is derived dynamically by
       the release workflow (`-r "$GITHUB_SERVER_URL/$GITHUB_REPOSITORY"`),
       and branches are fixed to main. Only adjust parserOpts here if the
       canonical commit form changes (keep in sync with
       .github/misc/commitlint.config.js).

6.8  .github/misc/.mega-linter.yml
     • SAST config (MegaLinter also fails the build; devskim bans C functions under include/ and src/)
       Optionally adjust linter settings for your coding style preferences.
       Required quality gates (clang-format/clang-tidy/gitleaks) live in
       .github/workflows/security-linters.yml and use the configs in
       .github/misc/.

6.9  .github/workflows/  (CI workflows)
     • Review and update workflow files if you need different trigger branches,
       additional CI matrix entries, or custom deployment steps.

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
SECTION 7 — GENERATION CHECKLIST  (for the agent to self-verify)
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

Before finishing, the agent MUST verify:

  [ ] metadata.json "build_cppstd" is "17" and "build_cstd" is "11".
  [ ] metadata.json "team" is "HeT-FTI" and "license" is "Apache-2.0".
  [ ] metadata.json "generate_modules_inplace" is false.
  [ ] metadata.json is consistent with all other Section 1 values.
  [ ] conandata.yml lists every dependency from Section 3.
  [ ] Every header in include/ has the Conan::ImportStart/End guard.
  [ ] Every source in src/ has the Conan::ImportStart/End guard.
  [ ] Every public symbol has Doxygen docstring with @exporter or @attacher.
  [ ] test_package/main.cpp benchmarks ALL public APIs with timing output.
  [ ] At least one unit test file exists per header in test_package/test/unit/.
  [ ] Stress test files exist for performance-critical paths in test/stress/.
  [ ] docs/doxygen/dox/mainpage.dox is rewritten for the new project.
  [ ] docs/doxygen/dox/demos/ holds a tutorial .dox with @example, and every
      file it @include-s exists.
  [ ] index.rst is concise (mini-paper style: background → method → quick
      start → results → license), readable in under 2 minutes.
  [ ] Long content is split into separate .rst files, not crammed in index.rst.
  [ ] For each non-English doc_language: .po files exist under
      docs/sphinx/locales/<lang>/LC_MESSAGES/ with FILLED translations.
  [ ] docs/images/ALL_title_card.png exists (placeholder or real artwork).
  [ ] README.md is updated with new project information.
  [ ] LICENSE and NOTICE are UNCHANGED from the template.
  [ ] No package-name literal left outside metadata.json.
  [ ] .github/misc/.releaserc.json needs no repositoryUrl edit (derived from git remote).
  [ ] If pybind11 enabled: api/python_bindings.cpp binds all public APIs.
  [ ] The whole project builds: conan create . -s build_type=Debug --build=missing
